title: Inductive Effect â€” +I and -I
notes: **Definition:** permanent displacement of sigma electrons along a carbon chain due to electronegativity difference between atoms.
**-I effect (electron withdrawing):** groups more electronegative than carbon pull electrons toward themselves. Examples: $-NO_2$, $-CN$, $-COOH$, halogens, $-CF_3$.

**+I effect (electron donating):** groups less electronegative than carbon push electrons away from themselves. Examples: alkyl groups ($-CH_3$, $-C_2H_5$), $-OCH_3$ (oxygen is electronegative but lone pairs donate).
**Effect on acidity:** -I groups increase acidity of carboxylic acids by stabilising the carboxylate anion. +I groups decrease acidity.
**Effect on basicity:** -I groups decrease basicity of amines by making the lone pair on N less available. +I groups increase basicity.
**Distance dependence:** inductive effect weakens rapidly with distance; it is significant only up to 3-4 bonds.
